review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked at the likely overlap with existing Mathlib concepts: FiniteReach (reachability within n steps), the Set.Finite/Finset characterisation (private finite_setOf_iff), and the measurability lemmas for ReflTransGen, Finite and Injective. I grepped Mathlib's Relation files and the rest of Mathlib for an n-step ReflTransGen characterisation, a bounded-reach relation, or a relation power with a ReflTransGen link, and found none. The only nearby result was reflTransGen_iff_eq_or_transGen, which is a different statement. I also found no Mathlib lemma of the form 'Set.Finite {i | p i} ↔ ∃ s : Finset, ...'. FiniteReach is also defined separately in OAI.Combinatorics.MatchingCount.Machines.TreeReach, but that is a different, typed, computational notion in a separate namespace, and this file's FiniteReach does not compete with it. The remaining declarations are measurability lemmas that are specific to this development, so I found no justified competing-concept finding. I am slightly uncertain whether Mathlib has an n-step relation power under a name I did not search for.
